verdict: OK to lend in Karnal dairy, but only to relocated or compliant value-added processors with tight monthly milk-payment and buyer-receipt controls; avoid the 44 dairies under final relocation notice until they shift.
title: Karnal dairy products: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What the business physically is
A Karnal dairy buys raw milk from village farmers, chills it, and converts it into milk, ghee, cheese or other value-added products. Cash comes in daily from milk sales and, for ghee and cheese, from distributors and retail chains. **The whole model turns on the spread between what you pay the farmer per fat unit and what the end market pays.** Farmers in five villages are demanding a Rs 12 per fat increase because tudi and khal feed have turned expensive [2], so when a proposal lands, check the procurement rate the unit actually pays versus the rate it can pass on; if the buyer contracts are fixed-price, ask how the spread survives a Rs 12 per fat rise.

## Where value and cash sit
Value sits in value-added products, not liquid milk. Milky Mist's Q2 FY27 revenue rose 42% to Rs 1,089.4 crore with EBITDA margin at 15.17% versus 13.95%, helped by product mix [4][6], and yogurt was its fastest-growing category [7]. **That is the peer template: ghee, cheese and curd carry the margin; plain milk carries the volume.** Working capital is short on the procurement side (farmers are paid on a short cycle) and longer on the distributor side, so monthly milk-payment discipline is the real credit test. Capex is chilling and processing equipment; collect from customer the unit's capacity and utilisation.

## What has changed now
Karnal's local stress is regulatory, not demand. **44 dairies have received a final notice to relocate or be sealed** [1], and an earlier sealing drive returned with only statements [3], so enforcement is live but uneven. Haryana GST collections are running +10.1% Apr-to-date versus India +6.1% [D], a genuine local tailwind. Nationally, bank credit is +26.3% YoY against output +5.1% [D], so pricing is competitive and weak units get refinanced rather than fixed. The CRISIL 13-14% growth call is from July 2024 and is dated [10]; treat it as history, not a forecast.

## Who to pursue and how to grow safely
**Pursue processors already on relocated or compliant premises, with a value-added product share and named buyers.** Avoid the 44 notice-hit units until relocation is documented [1]. Structure against receivables and milk payables, not land. Take monthly: farmer payment register, buyer receipts, fat-based procurement rate, and stock of ghee and cheese. If the unit sells only liquid milk, ask for the buyer list and contract tenure before sanctioning.

## Early-warning signs
- Farmer payout delays beyond the agreed cycle -> stop fresh disbursement and inspect.
- Procurement rate rising without a matching end-price change [2] -> rework the spread.
- Any sealing or relocation notice on the unit [1][3] -> freeze limit until compliance proof.
- Receivable days stretching past the peer norm -> ask for buyer confirmations.
